text: Gandalf visits Bilbo at Bag End.
The Unexpected Party.
Never quite remembering how it happened, Bilbo sets out from Bag End with Thorin and Company, bound for the Lonely Mountain.
Three trolls capture the Company; Gandalf outwits them, spurring an argument until sunrise turns them to stone.
The Company arrives at Rivendell, the Last Homely House west of the Mountains.
The Company rests in Rivendell while the Elves sing 'O! Tra-la-la-lally.'
Midsummer's Eve. Elrond reads the moon-letters on Thrór's map, revealing the secret entrance to the Lonely Mountain.
The Company departs Rivendell the day after Elrond fortuitously discovers the moon-letters on Thrór's map.
The Company is captured by Goblins.
Gandalf kills the Great Goblin, and the Dwarves escape. Bilbo finds the One Ring, trades riddles with Gollum, and escapes.
The Company, trapped by Wargs and Goblins, is rescued by the Eagles.
The Eagles carry the Company to the Carrock; they seek Beorn's hospitality.
Delighted by the death of the Great Goblin, Beorn lends the Company ponies for the journey to Mirkwood.
Gandalf leaves the Company at Mirkwood's edge to evict Sauron. The Company enters the forest on foot.
The Company crosses the Enchanted River. Bombur falls in.
The Company strays from the path, lured by lights in the forest.
Giant spiders capture the Dwarves; Bilbo rescues them.
Wood-elves capture the Company and imprison them.
Barrels Out of Bond. The Company escapes in barrels down the Forest River.
The Company arrives in Lake-town on Bilbo's birthday.
The Company receives a warm welcome in Lake-town.
The Company rows north from Lake-town.
The Company leaves the boats and crosses the Desolation of the Dragon.
The Company camps in the western valley.
On the Doorstep. Bilbo finds the hidden path to the secret door.
As the last light of Durin's Day fades, the thrush knocks and the secret door opens. Bilbo descends alone to speak with Smaug.
Bilbo returns to Smaug's lair. Roused to fury, the dragon scorches Lake-town and is slain by Bard.
News of Smaug's death reaches Gandalf, Beorn, and the Goblins.
The Elvenking's host marches out of Mirkwood, bound for the wealth of Erebor.
The Elven host turns south to aid Lake-town.
The Gathering of the Clouds. The Elves reach Lake-town; Dáin is summoned from the Iron Hills.
The Elves and Lake-men arrive at Dale as night falls.
Parley fails. The Lonely Mountain is besieged.
A Thief in the Night. Bilbo secretly brings the Arkenstone to Bard and the Elvenking, hoping to prevent war.
Dáin arrives. The Clouds Burst. Goblins and Wargs attack. The Battle of Five Armies.
There and Back Again. Gandalf and Bilbo leave the Lonely Mountain with Beorn.
Gandalf and Bilbo spend the winter at Beorn's house.
Bilbo returns home with mithril, gold, and the Ring. Sauron secretly returns to Mordor.
Bard rebuilds Dale. Gollum leaves the Mountains, hunting for his Precious.
Théoden is born.
Gandalf and Balin visit Bilbo in the Shire. 'You are a very fine person, Mr. Baggins, and I am very fond of you; but you are only quite a little fellow in a wide world after all!'
Finduilas, future mother of Boromir and Faramir, is born.
Sauron openly reveals himself and rebuilds Barad-dûr. Gollum heads toward Mordor. Aragorn learns his ancestry from Elrond and meets Arwen.
The White Council meets for the last time. Saruman falsely claims the One Ring was swept out to Sea. He fortifies Isengard and, jealous of Gandalf, begins spying on the Shire.
Mount Doom re-awakens in fire and ash. Anyone left in Ithilien flees.
Aragorn meets Gandalf for the first time.
Aragorn's years in disguise begin. Over the following decades, he serves Rohan and Gondor, and journeys in Rhûn, Harad, and even the borderlands of Mordor.
Frodo is born.
Denethor marries Finduilas of Dol Amroth.
Death of Bard. Bain, his son, becomes King.
Boromir is born.
Birth of Samwise Gamgee. Aragorn and Arwen betrothed upon Cerin Amroth in Lórien. Théoden becomes King of Rohan. Gollum meets Shelob.
Birth of Meriadoc Brandybuck.
Faramir is born.
Denethor II becomes Steward of Gondor, and steward of a palantír.
Finduilas, mother of Boromir and Faramir, dies young.
Against advice, Balin re-establishes a dwarf colony in Khazad-dûm.
Birth of Peregrin Took.
Éomer is born.
Balin slain; no dwarf in Moria survives to tell the tale.
Éowyn, sister of Éomer, is born.
Saruman falls under Sauron's influence through the palantír of Orthanc and turns traitor.

The Long-Expected Party. Bilbo vanishes before the entire Shire. Reluctantly but of his own free will, he leaves the Ring to Frodo. Gandalf suspects the Ring; he and Aragorn begin hunting for Gollum. The guard on the Shire is doubled.
Bilbo settles in Imladris and begins his Translations from the Elvish.
Gandalf begins visiting Frodo regularly, a habit that continues for the next four years.
Brand, grandson of Bard, becomes King of Dale.
Gandalf makes his last visit to Frodo for many years.

Over the next eight years, Gandalf and Aragorn redouble their hunt for Gollum. During this time, Gollum is captured in Mordor and taken to Barad-dûr. Arwen returns to Rivendell as travel grows more dangerous.

Sauron deliberately releases Gollum, who is captured by Aragorn in the Dead Marshes and taken to the Wood-elves in Mirkwood. In Minas Tirith, Gandalf finds Isildur's scroll. A servant of Sauron arrives in Dale, seeking news of hobbits.
The Shadow of the Past. Gandalf tests Bilbo's ring in the fire, revealing its inscription. The War of the Ring begins.
Gandalf tells Aragorn that Frodo plans to leave the Shire in September.
Sauron attacks Osgiliath; the Nazgûl cross the Anduin, hunting hobbits. Gollum escapes from the Wood-elves during a similar attack.
Gandalf leaves a letter for Frodo at the Prancing Pony, after Saruman tricks Radagast into sending Gandalf to Orthanc with news that the Nazgûl have crossed the Anduin seeking the Shire.
Boromir sets out from Minas Tirith, seeking the meaning of a prophetic dream that he and Faramir received.
Gandalf seeks Saruman's help and instead finds himself imprisoned atop Orthanc.
All trace of Gollum is lost. Hunted by Elves and Sauron, he hides in Moria, unable to find his way out.
Gwaihir rescues Gandalf, sent by Radagast with news. The Black Riders cross the Fords of Isen under new orders from Sauron.
Disguised as a beggar, Gandalf is refused entry to Edoras.
Gandalf gains an audience with Théoden, who orders him to leave Rohan within a day. The Black Riders reach Isengard, where Saruman deceives them.
Gandalf meets Shadowfax and begins taming him. Gríma Wormtongue reveals the Shire's location to the Black Riders, exposing the extent of Saruman's treachery.
The Black Riders overwhelm the Rangers guarding the Shire's southern border. Frodo turns fifty.
Four Black Riders enter the Shire before dawn. By nightfall, one reaches Hobbiton, narrowly missing Frodo as he leaves Bag End.
High Elves providentially drive off a Black Rider and give the hobbits shelter for the night.
Farmer Maggot gives the hobbits a ride to Bucklebury Ferry after encountering a Black Rider.
The hobbits enter the Old Forest. Tom Bombadil rescues them from Old Man Willow.
The hobbits spend a second night with Tom Bombadil.
A Barrow-wight captures the hobbits; Bombadil rescues them again. Merry picks up a blade that could help kill a Witch-king.
The hobbits meet Strider at the Prancing Pony.
Black Riders ransack the inn during the night. The hobbits and Strider leave that morning.
Frodo sees distant flashes in the night as Gandalf battles the Nazgûl on Weathertop.
The Black Riders attack. The Witch-king wounds Frodo with a Morgul-blade.
Frodo rides a pony, growing weaker by the day.
Glorfindel encounters three Nazgûl. 'They withdrew and I pursued them.' He leaves a token that the bridge is safe to cross.
The Company finds Glorfindel's token and crosses the bridge. Frodo worsens, drawing closer to the wraith-world.
The Company passes Bilbo's trolls. Glorfindel (Arwen in the movie) finds them at dusk.
Flight to the Ford. Frodo rides Glorfindel's horse.
Alone and near death, Frodo defies the Nazgûl. The Ringwraiths hesitate; the flood sweeps them away.
Frodo wakes with Gandalf at his bedside.
The Council of Elrond. Luckily, precisely the right people are in Rivendell on separate errands at the same time.
Autumn wanes. December passes in preparation: scouts are sent, and counsel is sought.
The Fellowship of the Ring is formed. Sensing the hand of Providence, Elrond correctly agrees to the stupid plan: send Merry and Pippin.
The Fellowship departs Rivendell.
The Ring Goes South.
The Fellowship crosses into Hollin. Spooked by crebain, they spend the day hiding.
The Fellowship attempts the Redhorn Pass. Snow and bitter cold force them back.
Wolves attack in the night. By morning, the bodies have vanished.
'Speak, friend, and enter.' The Fellowship enters Moria. Gollum begins trailing the Ring-bearer.
A Journey in the Dark.
The Bridge of Khazad-dûm. Gandalf falls.
Elves escort the blindfolded Fellowship into Lothlórien.
Galadriel and Celeborn welcome the Fellowship to Caras Galadhon.
The Fellowship rests and grieves for Gandalf, beginning to heal in Lórien.
Gandalf pursues the Balrog to the peak of Zirak-zigil.
Gandalf slays the Balrog—and dies. As do all who kill a Balrog.
The Fellowship continues to recover in Lórien.
The Mirror of Galadriel. Frodo offers her the Ring, which she refuses. Gandalf returns.
Farewell to Lórien. Gollum follows the Fellowship downstream.
The Fellowship takes to the Great River. Boats: far quicker than walking.
Orc archers ambush the Fellowship at night. Legolas shoots down the winged steed of a Nazgûl.
The Fellowship passes between the Argonath and camps at Parth Galen, uncertain which path to take next.
Breaking of the Fellowship. Boromir tries to take the Ring. Frodo and Sam set out east alone.
Breaking of the Fellowship. Boromir dies defending Merry and Pippin; Orcs capture them. Aragorn sets out in pursuit.
Frodo and Sam lose their way among the barren slopes and stony ravines of the Emyn Muil.
The Three Hunters race across the plains of Rohan.
The Taming of Sméagol. Frodo and Sam capture Gollum, who leads them out of the Emyn Muil.
The Three Hunters meet the Riders of Rohan and learn the Orcs have been destroyed. Éomer lends them horses.
Gollum leads Frodo and Sam into the Dead Marshes.
Aragorn meets Gandalf the White in Fangorn. They ride for Edoras.
Frodo and Sam reach the far edge of the Dead Marshes.
Gandalf heals Théoden. The Rohirrim ride to war.
The Battle of the Hornburg. Elves only appear in the cinema.
Frodo and Sam hide in the slag-mounds at the edge of the Desolation of the Morannon.
Victorious, Théoden and Gandalf set out from Helm's Deep for Isengard.
The Black Gate is shut. Gollum leads Frodo and Sam south in search of another way in.
Saruman refuses to yield Orthanc. Pippin looks into the palantír; a Nazgûl flies overhead. Gandalf rides for Minas Tirith with Pippin.
Of Herbs and Stewed Rabbit.
Aragorn reveals himself to Sauron through the palantír. Théoden rides for Dunharrow; Aragorn follows with the Grey Company.
Faramir’s Rangers capture Frodo and Sam. Faramir immediately refuses the Ring, unlike the movie detour to Osgiliath.
Aragorn reaches Dunharrow at nightfall. Gandalf and Pippin see the beacons of Gondor alight.
Frodo saves Gollum from execution at the Forbidden Pool; Gollum feels betrayed. Faramir lets them leave Henneth Annûn.
Aragorn takes the Paths of the Dead at daybreak. That night, at the Stone of Erech, he summons the Dead Men to fulfill an oath sworn three thousand years earlier.
Frodo reaches the Morgul-road at dusk.
Gandalf and Pippin reach Minas Tirith. Darkness begins to flow out of Mordor.
The Dawnless Day. Frodo sees the army of Minas Morgul march out.
The Dawnless Day. Rohan musters for war. Gandalf rescues Faramir outside the gates of Minas Tirith.
Gollum visits Shelob. Seeing Frodo asleep, he nearly repents. Tragically, Sam wakes and harshly interrupts.
Denethor orders Faramir to defend Osgiliath.
Gollum leads Frodo and Sam into Shelob's Lair.
Aragorn drives the enemy south toward Pelargir. Faramir retreats to the Causeway Forts.
Shelob stings Frodo; Sam wounds her in return. Sam takes the Ring. Orcs carry Frodo away. The Choices of Master Samwise.
The Pelennor is overrun. Faramir is wounded; Denethor’s hope fails. Aragorn captures the Corsair fleet at Pelargir and releases the Dead.
Sam finds Frodo alive in the Tower of Cirith Ungol.
Minas Tirith is besieged. Théoden takes a shortcut.
Frodo and Sam escape and flee north along the Morgai. Sam sees a star.

At dawn, the Witch-king breaks the City’s gates. The horns of Rohan sound. The Battle of the Pelennor Fields begins. Denethor burns; Théoden falls; Éowyn and Merry destroy the Witch-king. Aragorn arrives with the fleet to save the City.
From the Morgai, Frodo looks out over Sauron’s armies toward Mount Doom.
The Last Debate. The Captains of the West plan a diversionary assault on the Black Gate, drawing Sauron’s attention from Frodo.
The Land of Shadow.
The Host of the West musters for the march on Mordor.
Frodo and Sam are swept into an Orc-march.
The Host of the West marches out from Minas Tirith.
Frodo and Sam escape the Orcs and resume their journey along the road toward Barad-dûr.
The Host of the West marches through Ithilien.
Frodo and Sam leave the road and turn south toward Mount Doom.
Frodo and Sam cast away their gear.
Aragorn sends the faint-hearted back to retake Cair Andros.
Frodo and Sam make their final journey to the feet of Mount Doom.
The Host camps in the Desolation of the Morannon, within sight of the Black Gate.
Sam carries Frodo up the mountain. At the Cracks of Doom, Frodo claims the Ring for himself. Gollum bites it from his hand and falls into the fire. The Ring is destroyed; Sauron falls.
The Black Gate opens. The Host of the West is surrounded. Eucatastrophe: the Ring is destroyed, and Sauron falls.
